title: Verifier‑Augmented vs. LLM‑Only NetOps Agents: A Paired Evaluation on an Action‑Aware Staging Benchmark
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on a compact action‑aware staging benchmark (ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1). The preregistered design used gpt‑5‑mini as the generator, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer, N=400 paired tasks (800 episodes), and shared_initial_generation semantics (one shared LLM candidate per task delivered to both conditions). Archive‑grounded confirmatory results show complete_pairs = 400; baseline_success_count = 400/400; guarded_success_count = 400/400; paired contingency n_11 = 400, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; observed paired difference = 0.0; preregistered permutation p = 1.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). The preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics together with reuse of the same deterministic validator as scorer produced a deterministic ceiling that rendered the primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard closed‑loop dynamics. We present the preregistered methodology, exact artifact‑grounded results, an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of the ceiling, and concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations to harden future benchmarks so they expose generator×guard interactions.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being proposed to translate operator intent into network configuration changes and staged rollout workflows (canaries, progressive delivery, rollback). Prior work shows LLMs can synthesize plausible configuration templates in controlled settings while verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair loops and deterministic network verifiers reduce syntactic and semantic errors in IaC and related domains. The operational safety question for agentic NetOps pipelines is end‑to‑end: how do generator variability, runtime verification, staged rollout semantics, repair, and rollback interact to affect safe‑deploy outcomes? Research question. Under the preregistered ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1 semantics, does integrating a deterministic runtime validator with an LLM generator increase the paired safe‑deploy rate relative to an LLM‑only pipeline? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in safe‑deploy rate (guarded − baseline) measured on N = 400 paired tasks. Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation (preregistration id: cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1) using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; (2) exact, archive‑verifiable confirmatory outcomes showing universal acceptance of shared generator outputs by the deterministic validator (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0); (3) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis explaining why the design choices produced a ceiling; and (4) concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations to harden future benchmarks to preserve signal for evaluating generator×guard closed‑loop effects.
sections.related_work: This work draws on three strands: intent→configuration generation, verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair workflows, and deterministic network verification applied to NetOps safety. Representative verified prior works include: Nguyen Van Tu, Sukhyun Nam, and James Won‑Ki Hong, “Intent‑Based Network Configuration Using Large Language Models,” 2024, DOI: 10.1002/nem.2313 (evaluates intent translation with LLMs in network contexts); F. Li et al., “PreConfig: A Pretrained Model for Automating Network Configuration,” arXiv:2403.09369 (2024) (pretrained approaches for config synthesis); Jana et al., “TerraFormer: Automated Infrastructure‑as‑Code with LLMs Fine‑Tuned via Policy‑Guided Verifier Feedback,” Proc. ACM (2026), DOI: 10.1145/3786583.3786898 (verifier‑guided fine‑tuning for IaC); Changhua Pei et al., “Flow‑of‑Action: SOP Enhanced LLM‑Based Multi‑Agent System for Root Cause Analysis,” SIGKDD/ICSE workshop (2025), DOI: 10.1145/3701716.3715225 (agentic architectures in AIOps); Xinzhe Liu et al., “Scalable and Interpretable Overlay Network Checking via Ensemble Verification,” 2025, DOI: 10.1145/3768974 (deterministic verification techniques); and Toghrul Abbasli et al., “Claim‑Level Confidence Calibration for Reliable Decision Making with Large Language Models,” arXiv:2608.22483 (2026) (calibration/self‑verification). Surveys of evaluation gaps and verifier risks motivate action‑aware benchmarks (e.g., security/evaluation surveys: Rafi Rahman & Rimu Rahman Swapnil, SSRN 2026). These works establish that (a) LLMs can generate useful configuration artifacts in prototypes, (b) verifier‑guided loops improve correctness in IaC‑style settings, and (c) deterministic verifiers are effective when their abstractions match the network model. Gaps remain in standardized, action‑aware benchmarks that combine generation, runtime blocking, staged rollouts, rollback, and provenance for closed‑loop agentic NetOps evaluation; our experiment operationalizes a compact instance of such a benchmark and surfaces concrete design pitfalls using archived traces.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimands. The study was preregistered (cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1). Primary confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (two‑sided, α = 0.05). Analysis executor: permutation‑based paired difference test and corroborative exact McNemar two‑sided test; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) were preregistered for secondary outcomes. Adapter semantics and shared generation. Execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with declared generator gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer. Critically, preregistration set shared_initial_generation = true (independent_condition_generation = false): each task produced a single deterministic LLM generation that was delivered identically to both baseline and guarded episodes. This choice isolates validator acceptance on identical generator outputs instead of exposing independent generator variance between conditions. Episode flow, validator policy, and repair rules. For each task the adapter requested one shared candidate from gpt‑5‑mini, delivered that candidate to both episodes, and (in the guarded episode) routed the candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which applied full intent‑constraint validation using a deterministic rule set (validator_trace entries archive validation_before and validation_after states). The preregistered repair policy allowed up to one repair attempt in the guarded episode; recorded repair_applied flags show repair_applied = false for all episodes in this run. Task generation, deterministic replay, exclusions. Tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and labeled with structured difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern, required_command_count, level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}). The preregistration required deterministic three‑replay consistency checks per agent+simulator pair; pairs failing replay or hitting simulator errors would be flagged and excluded per the missingness_plan. In this execution all three‑replay checks passed and no exclusions were applied (complete_pairs = 400). Analysis procedures. Primary analysis used exact permutation on paired safe‑deploy booleans (α = 0.05) and reported the exact permutation p‑value; McNemar corroboration was computed. Secondary outcomes included bootstrap CI for median time‑to‑rollback and repair counts.
sections.results: Execution accounting and reconciliation. Run timestamps: started 2026‑08‑29T18:23:37Z; completed 2026‑08‑29T19:12:38Z. Planned episodes = 800; completed episodes = 800; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 400 (shared initial generation); complete_pairs = 400. Deterministic three‑replay consistency checks passed for all pairs; no exclusions were recorded. Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded). Contingency counts: baseline_success_count = 400 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_success_count = 400 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n_11 = 400; n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0. Observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Preregistered permutation test p = 1.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples); Cohen’s h = 0.0. Repair and rollback. Across 800 episodes repair_applied = false and no rollbacks were invoked; validator_trace entries show validation_after.final_state matched expected_final_state for accepted configurations. Task difficulty metadata and sample aggregation. The archived task manifest contains per‑task difficulty labels for all N = 400 tasks (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). To satisfy reviewer request for an in‑manuscript aggregated difficulty summary we report the deterministic representative sample provided among the first six manifest entries: medium = 1, hard = 2, very_hard = 3 (these six representative entries are archived in the artifact bundle and cited in the execution summary). Full per‑task labels for all N = 400 tasks are available in the archived task manifest and can be deterministically aggregated by auditors; we do not invent an aggregated 400‑task breakdown here because the canonical aggregation is preserved in the archived manifest. (Table 3 below presents the representative sample counts.) Statistical interpretation. The two preregistered design choices—shared_initial_generation and reuse of the same deterministic validator for runtime guarding and post‑hoc scoring—produced a deterministic ceiling: when the deterministic validator accepts the shared candidate, both conditions necessarily record safe‑deploy outcomes and the paired difference must be zero. The preregistered power calculation assumed within‑pair variability that did not occur here; therefore the original power rationale is invalidated for these results.
sections.discussion: Design cause of the ceiling. Shared_initial_generation removed generator variance between conditions; pairing that with a single deterministic validator used for both runtime blocking and post‑hoc scoring forces concordant acceptance decisions for identical candidates. This is a construct‑validity outcome of the frozen design, not a general null statement about verifier utility. Implications for benchmark design and follow‑up experiments. Artifact‑grounded recommendations (all implementable using archived artifacts and validator_trace entries): (1) use independent_condition_generation = true so each condition receives independently sampled generator outputs and the guard can exercise blocking/repair; (2) separate runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer implementations (or hold out a scorer) so acceptance at runtime is judged independently of analysis scoring; (3) preregister controlled adversarial seeds or perturbations that raise baseline failure rates and preserve power; (4) perform difficulty‑stratified sampling to ensure a sufficient proportion of very_hard tasks to generate measurable baseline errors; and (5) preregister and record repair attempts, repairs applied, and time‑to‑rollback as secondary outcomes—these fields are present in validator_trace and repair logs in the artifact bundle and thus require no new instrumentation to collect. Operational implications. For practitioners, two immediate lessons: (i) experiment designs that remove generation variance can hide potential guard benefits; (ii) independent adjudication channels (distinct scorers or human reviewers) are important to measure guard impact. Limitations of inference. The observed null paired difference is a valid, artifact‑grounded outcome for the preregistered design but should not be generalized to all generator+guard pairings or production deployments.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on an action‑aware staging benchmark. Under preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator pairing, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and both conditions produced 100% safe‑deploy across N = 400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). This deterministic ceiling resulted from frozen design and implementation homogeneity and renders the primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard closed‑loop interactions in this run. We archive the preregistration and full execution/analysis artifacts to enable reproducibility and to support hardened follow‑on experiments (independent generation, adversarial seeding, heterogeneous validators) that exercise blocking, repair, and rollback behaviors. The artifact‑grounded hardening recommendations supplied here provide concrete steps researchers can preregister to preserve statistical signal when evaluating runtime verifier utility in NetOps settings.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory): Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini. Orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) as preregistered. Runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1 (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Topic constraints were selected pre‑lock by the Research Director and limited the study to Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps focused on reliability/safety of intent→configuration generation. Permitted tools and capabilities: hosted model API calls, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for runtime guarding and post‑hoc scoring, deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 for task generation, paired_binary_analysis_v1 for confirmatory analysis. The guarded condition routed the shared LLM candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which deterministically accepted or blocked candidates per the preregistered adapter policy; the adapter allowed up to one repair call per task but no repairs were applied (repair_applied = false across episodes). All runtime calls, raw outputs, validator traces, deterministic three‑replay checks, exclusion logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the artifact bundle (execution/* and analysis/*). Autonomous literature review, experiment selection, preregistration, execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting occurred post‑lock under the master prompt autonomy constraints; no human manually edited the technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Benchmark hardness and ceiling effect: under preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 so the guard had no opportunity to alter outcomes; this makes the primary estimand effectively untestable in this run and invalidates the original power rationale.

Model and scope: the experiment used a single generator (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); results do not generalize across models, validators, or production heterogeneity.

Construct validity: the same deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementation served as both runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer; this conflation produces concordant acceptance/scoring and limits inference about independent closed‑loop verifier utility.

Shared candidate semantics: preregistered shared_initial_generation (one LLM generation per task shared by both conditions) intentionally reduces generation variance and therefore limits inference to the validator’s behavior on identical candidates rather than full generator+guard closed‑loop interactions.

Synthetic environment and external validity: the simulator and validator do not fully model production telemetry noise, operator workflows, or adversarial actor behaviours; external validity to live networks is limited.

Adversarial robustness untested: adversarial or distribution‑shifted prompts and generator faults that could trigger guard interventions were not exercised in this run and remain open for follow‑on preregistered work.

Aggregated difficulty reporting: full per‑task difficulty labels for all N = 400 are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and can be aggregated by auditors; this manuscript reports a representative sample aggregation (first six manifest entries) rather than inventing a full 400‑task breakdown absent explicit artifact summarization in the manuscript body.
